name: Whitefly
description_damage: Adult is white and very small; it looks like a miniature moth. They typically feed on the undersides of leaves, flying up in clouds when disturbed. Immature stages are flat, oval, white to greenish, and semitransparent. Eggs are white and laid singly on the lower leaf surface. Whiteflies feed by sucking sap from the plants. Damaged leaves wilt, turn yellow or brown, and may drop, all of which reduces photosynthetic area and weakens the plant. Plants may be stunted by severe infestations. Whiteflies also produce honeydew, which may attract ants or become covered with a growth of sooty mold.

management.cultural: Inspect new plants before purchase: infestations often are introduced. Encourage natural enemies such as ladybird beetles, spiders, and parasitic wasps. Avoid use of broad-spectrum insecticides which reduce populations of these.
